edition.copy_text: Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI

source_text: Εἶτα εἴ τις δύναται ὡς ἐν ἱστορίας σχήματι, ἐχούσης μέν τι καὶ καθ᾿ αὑτὴν ἀληθὲς ἐμφαινούσης δέ τι καὶ ἀπόῤῥητον, ἰδέτω καὶ τοὺς τὴν ἐξ ἀρχῆς διάλεκτον τετηρηκότας, τῷ μὴ κεκινηκέναι „ἀπ᾿ ἀνατολῶν“ μένοντας ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ τῇ ἀνατολικῇ διαλέκτῳ· καὶ νοείτω τούτους μόνους γεγονέναι μερίδα κυρίου καὶ λαὸν αὐτοῦ τὸν καλούμενον „Ἰακὼβ,“ γεγονέναι δὲ καὶ „σχοίνισμα κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ Ἰσραήλ“· καὶ οὗτοι μόνοι ἐπιστατείσθωσαν ὑπὸ ἄρχοντος, οὐκ ἐπὶ κολάσει παρειληφότος τοὺς ὑπ᾿ αὐτῷ ὥσπερ οἱ ἄλλοι. βλεπέτω δ᾿ ὁ δυνάμενος ὡς ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἐν τῇ τούτων πολιτείᾳ τῶν τεταγμένων κατὰ τὴν διαφέρουσαν μερίδα τῷ κυρίῳ γινομένας ἁμαρτίας, πρότερον μὲν ἀνεκτὰς καὶ τοιαύτας, ὡς μὴ πάντῃ ἀξίους εἶναι αὐτοὺς τοῦ ἐγκαταλείπεσθαι, ὕστερον δὲ πλείονας μὲν ἀλλ᾿ ἔτι ἀνεκτάς· καὶ τοῦτ᾿ ἐπὶ πλείονα χρόνον νοῶν γινόμενον καὶ ἀεὶ θεραπείαν προσαγομένην καὶ ἐκ διαλειμμάτων τούτους ἐπιστρέφοντας, ὁράτω αὐτοὺς καταλειπομένους κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῶν ἁμαρτανομένων τοῖς λαχοῦσι τὰς ἄλλας χώρας, πρότερον μὲν ἐπὶ τὸ ἔλαττον αὐτοὺς κολασθέντας καὶ τίσαντας δίκην, ὡσπερεὶ παιδευθέντας, ἐπανελθεῖν εἰς τὰ οἰκεῖα· ὕστερον δὲ βλεπέτω αὐτοὺς παραδιδομένους χαλεπωτέροις ἄρχουσιν, ὡς ἂν ὀνομάσαιεν αἱ γραφαὶ, Ἀσσυρίοις εἶτα Βαβυλωνίοις. εἶτα προσαγομένων θεραπειῶν ὁράτω τούτους οὐδὲν ἧττον αὔξοντας τὰ ἁμαρτανόμενα καὶ διὰ τοῦτ᾿ ἐπισπειρομένους ὑπὸ τῶν διαρπαζόντων αὐτοὺς ἀρχόντων τῶν λοιπῶν ἐθνῶν ταῖς ἄλλαις μερίσιν. ὁ δ᾿ ἄρχων αὐτῶν ἐπίτηδες παροράτω διαρπαζομένους αὐτοὺς ὑπὸ τῶν ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀρχόντων· ἵνα καὶ αὐτὸς εὐλόγως, ὡσπερεὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐκδικῶν, λαβὼν ἐξουσίαν ἀποσπάσαι τῶν λοιπῶν ἐθνῶν οὓς ἂν δύνηται, τὸ τοιοῦτο ποιήσῃ καὶ νόμους τε αὐτοῖς θῆται καὶ βίον ὑποδείξῃ καθ᾿ ὃν βιωτέον· ἵνα αὐτοὺς ἀναγάγῃ ἐπὶ τέλος, ἐφ᾿ ὅπερ ἀνῆγε τοὺς μὴ ἁμαρτάνοντας ἀπὸ τοῦ προτέρου ἔθνους.
thought_title: The Lord’s portion and its exile
pass_a_gloss: Then, if anyone can, as in the figure (σχῆμα) of a history having something true even by itself but showing (ἐμφαίνω) something also unspeakable (ἀπόρρητον), let him see also those who have kept the language from the beginning (ἐξ ἀρχῆς διάλεκτος), by not having moved 'from the east' remaining in the east and the eastern language; and let him understand these alone to have become the portion (μερίς) of the Lord and his people called 'Jacob', and to have become 'the measured lot (σχοίνισμα) of his inheritance, Israel'; and let these alone be governed (ἐπιστατέω) by a ruler (ἄρχων) not having received (παραλαμβάνω) those under him for punishment (ἐπὶ κολάσει) as the others. Let the able one see, as among humans, in the polity (πολιτεία) of these ranked (τάσσω) in the portion belonging (διαφέρω) to the Lord, sins (ἁμαρτίαι) happening, at first bearable (ἀνεκτός) and such that they were not wholly worthy of being forsaken (ἐγκαταλείπω), later more numerous but still bearable; and understanding this happening for a longer time and healing (θεραπεία) always applied (προσάγω) and at intervals (ἐκ διαλειμμάτων) these turning back (ἐπιστρέφω), let him see them left (καταλείπω) in proportion (ἀναλογία) to the sins to those who obtained by lot (λαγχάνω) the other lands, at first punished to a lesser degree and paying penalty, as if disciplined (παιδεύω), returning (ἐπανέρχομαι) to their own; but later let him see them handed over to harsher rulers, as the Scriptures would name, Assyrians then Babylonians. Then, with healings applied, let him see these no less increasing (αὔξω) the sins and on this account being sown among (ἐπισπείρω) by the rulers of the remaining nations who plunder (διαρπάζω) them into the other portions. And let their ruler purposely (ἐπίτηδες) overlook (παροράω) them being plundered by the rulers in the remaining nations, so that he too reasonably (εὐλόγως), as if avenging (ἐκδικέω) himself, having taken authority (ἐξουσία) to draw off (ἀποσπάω) from the remaining nations whom he can, may do such a thing and lay down laws for them and show a life according to which one must live (βιωτέον); so that he may lead them up (ἀνάγω) to the end (τέλος) to which he was leading up those not sinning from the former nation.

pass_b_english: Next, if anyone can, as under the figure of a history which has something true in itself and yet also points to something secret, let him see also those who kept the original language: because they did not move “from the east,” they remained in the east and in the eastern language. And let him understand that these alone became the Lord’s portion and his people called “Jacob,” and became also “Israel, the measured lot of his inheritance” (Deuteronomy 32:9). And let these alone be governed by a ruler who did not receive those under him for punishment, as the others did.

Let him who is able see also the sins, such as happen among human beings, committed in the commonwealth of those assigned to the portion that belongs to the Lord. At first they were tolerable, and of such a kind that the people did not altogether deserve to be forsaken; later they were more numerous, but still tolerable. And understanding that this went on for a long time, and that healing was always being applied, and that at intervals they turned back, let him see them abandoned, in proportion to their sins, to those who had received the other lands by lot: at first punished lightly and paying the penalty, and then, as if they had been disciplined, returning to their own land. But later let him see them handed over to harsher rulers, whom the Scriptures would name Assyrians and then Babylonians.

Then, though remedies were applied, let him see them increasing their sins none the less, and for this reason scattered among the other portions by the rulers of the other nations who plundered them. And let their own ruler deliberately overlook their being plundered by the rulers in the other nations, so that he too, with good reason and as if avenging himself, may receive authority to draw away from the other nations all whom he can, and may do so, and give them laws and show them the life they must live, in order to lead them up to the goal to which he used to lead those of the former nation who did not sin.
notes: Deuteronomy 32:9 (LXX) is taken up again from 5.29; 'measured lot' kept for σχοίνισμα. Origen continues the third-person imperatives ('let him see ... let their ruler overlook'), kept as such. The cycle of sin, light punishment and return probably reflects the pattern of Judges, and the exiles to Assyria and Babylon (2 Kings 17 and 25), but these are narrative summaries, not quotations, so no verse is cited inline. ἐπισπειρομένους ('sown in among', 'scattered among') rendered 'scattered among'; the construction ὑπὸ τῶν διαρπαζόντων αὐτοὺς ἀρχόντων τῶν λοιπῶν ἐθνῶν ταῖς ἄλλαις μερίσιν read as agent (rulers of the other nations) plus destination (the other portions). ὡς ἐν ἀνθρώποις taken as 'such as happen among human beings'. ἐπὶ πλείονα χρόνον rendered 'for a long time' (comparative used loosely). 'Ruler' (ἄρχων) of the Lord's portion is left lowercase, since Origen speaks in figure and does not name him here; in 5.32 he identifies the one more powerful than all rulers with Jesus.
